title: OXO Good Grips 5-lb Food Scale with Pull-Out Display,Black
description:
About this item
5-pound-capacity Food Scale measures in 1/8-ounce and 1-gram increments
Display pulls away from base to avoid shadowing from plates or bowls
Zero function tares Scale before adding additional ingredients

reviews_5s:
I had no idea the pull out face would be so useful. if I ever have to buy another scale, that will be a requirement. I do wish I would have went for the larger one because I find myself wanting to weigh slightly heavier things and there's no point in having to scales so buying one now feels excessive. Get the bigger one if you think this might be an issue for you.This is the best kitchen scale ive ever had. It works great. The batteries do seem to drain fast but that is the only minor issue I have had so far.Excellent food scale. I like that it's small and doesn't take much room, just pull it out from it's base to weigh your food. Put your plate on the scale, hit the lb/kg button on the right to go to '0' weight. Then add your food. It's very well made and I've used it every day for over a year and I haven't needed to change the battery yet.I love this scale. It’s perfect! I love how it stays on while I am measuring all that I need without having to worry about it turning off! And for the other comments of people saying it doesn’t turn off, well it’s not rocket science! All you do is press the zero button and that is your off switch. It’s super easy to use and the buttons are functional. This is very durable.This scale works great!I like this scale when I make bread, I put a plastic bowl on it and sift the flour right into it.

It isn't as precise for tiny amounts but I have a small scale when I need that. I have some calibration weights and found that one gram accuracy is pushing it. But a cook should have two scales anyway, one with a larger capacity and one with a smaller one. I like that you can pull the display out and that it doesn't go off right away. I got the 5lb one because I don't really need to weigh 11 pounds of anything. The platform is removable for cleaning but it takes quite a bit of force to get off and on. I haven't really had to clean it yet, I might never have to. It's nice to know I can.

I use weigh boats and other containers, I don't just put stuff on it to weighI have been searching for a long time to find a scale that does NOT have an irritating, short timeout. Finally, after 2 weeks with this OXO 5lb. Food scale I think I've found one.

Here's how it works. After 5 minutes of inactivity the illuminated display goes dim. But it still recalls the weight of whatever is on it for another 10 minutes. Tap the weighed item with your finger and the display lights up instantly with perfect memory of your weighed item, and the entire timeout sequence restarts anew.

If you leave it unused for more than 15 minutes the scales shuts down and the memory of the weighed item is lost - it will read Zero if you turn it on again. If you have good lighting, and good eyes, you can actually read the scale during the last 10 minutes of the timeout. It's very dim, but you can see the digits if you look closely.

There is a feature that keeps the scale on forever (or a bug depending on how you feel about this). If you zero out an item on the scale (say your steel mixing bowl) and remove it, the scale will naturally read a negative amount. What's interesting is that as long as it's reading a negative amount it never turns itself off (well, I waited over 30 minutes and didn't turn off, so I am making an assumption here). I think the idea is that the scale knows it is in use, and waits patiently for you to return with your bowl and get back to work. I love this feature, but from reading other reviews it's clear others do not.

Another nice thing - the display lights up - this is better than simple backlighting as each segment of each digit glows. The scale is accurate to 1 gram (perfectly matched out existing scale during my testing). This scale is cheaper than another OXO model that has a stainless steel rather than plastic weighing tray. We have loads of stainless steel in our kitchen at the moment and I am perfectly content with the all plastic design. Of course if you need 10 lb. capacity, rather than 5 lb. then you will want the stainless steel model.

For those among us that are capable of manually turning off appliances this may be one of the best 5 lb. scales on the market.I got tickets to America’s test kitchen live in Cincinnati late last year and they specifically said this was the best scale on the market. My favorite feature is the fact that you can pull it display out of it if there’s a large bowl blocking your view and that’s why I bought it.I recently upgraded to the OXO Good Grips 5-lb Food Scale with Pull-Out Display, and it’s made a huge difference in my cooking and baking. Here’s why this scale has become an essential tool in my kitchen:

Convenient Design
Pull-Out Display: The pull-out display is a game-changer! No more struggling to read the measurements when using large bowls or plates. It makes the whole process so much easier.
Compact and Sleek: The scale is compact and doesn’t take up much counter space. It’s also lightweight, making it easy to move around or store.

Accurate Measurements
I’ve used this scale for everything from baking to portioning out meals, and it’s consistently accurate. It’s a great tool for keeping my recipes precise and my portions controlled.

Easy to Clean
The flat surface is super easy to wipe down, so I don’t have to worry about crumbs or spills causing a mess.

Comparison
Compared to my old Etekcity scale, the OXO Good Grips scale has a much more user-friendly design. The pull-out display and ease of cleaning set it apart, making it a better choice for everyday use.

Conclusion
If you’re in the market for a reliable and convenient kitchen scale, the OXO Good Grips 5-lb Food Scale is a fantastic choice. It’s accurate, easy to use, and the pull-out display is a standout feature. I highly recommend it to anyone looking to upgrade their kitchen tools!Tested via weighing water and it was accurate and precise. Love the ability to pull out the display; I am often setting big plates and bowls on top. Makes cooking so much cleaner when I don't have a million measuring cups over the counter and them dripping or spilling whatever they contained on the counter when I set the empty measuring cup or whatever down.
reviews_1s:
I had an OXO scale for over 5 years. until it finally wouldn't work. I ordered another one recently but had to return it as it didnt work properly. I got another one. in April. The quality of my
first scale 5 years ago was superior to the new one that I recently purchased and had to return for another one.
So disappointed
.It's cheaply made. I pulled off the plastic cover for the labels on the read out, and the whole strip came off. It's not the same quality of scale I bought years ago from OXO. Very disappointed.There is a giant sticker on the back informing me I'm not legally allowed to use my scale. I'm not sure who decided I'm not allowed to use the item I bought, but if I'm not allowed to use it I'll return it. I know this isn't the actual point of the sticker, but the fact there's an authority that forces them to place this on their product is abhorrent and everything wrong with society. I tried to remove the sticker yet am not able to do that either. Back it goes. Don't lecture me in all caps in a manner I can't remove.Worst scale I’ve ever owned, you can weigh something three times and get three different numbers, totally useless! If I could give it zero stars I would.Needed to replace my old XOXO scale that I had for at least 10 years after the batteries corroded. I bought the new scale and did not get around to pulling it out of the box until now. Put in the batteries that came with the scale. Would not turn on. Tried brand new batteries that I had in my fridge. No sign of life. Going straight to the electronic recycling box at Staples. Buyer beware!The display is advertised to turn off after a certain amount of time but that does not happen. What does happen is the scale stays on all night and you end up having to change the four AAA batteries every month.

I ended up getting a replacement through OXO customer support and had the same exact issue. Look at the other reviews and you can see this is an ongoing and known issue with this make/model of scale.

When the scale works it's lovely but changing the batteries every single month is a huge problem and most scales I've used in the past only need them changed once a year or two.The decimal (.0) is only showing on Pound not on Gram. It was a hard time to measure ingredients without it most especially if the recipe ingredients are showing in grams. It was time consuming for me to compute it on lbs while cooking/baking.When I decided to pay twice as much for the OXO scale, I expected a robust, ergonomic and detail-oriented device, just as I am used to getting from the brand.

This is a lightweight, flimsy, cheaply-made scale. It is all plastic without the rubber grip pads that have made OXO their name. I had a glass-top scale that I could've replaced with an identical one for just over half the price of this thing - it felt twice as robust and had twice the cachet.Every time when I use, it showed "Lo" battery and went off. I thought it was our batteries so I kept buy new batteries for a month to replace. But still kept doing same thing. Finally I realized it's not batteries it's the product issue. I found it after a moth later and I can not return the product now. Spent an hour how to return or request replacement. Being Prime Member didn't help.
:(I bought this scale as a replacement for one that was giving inaccurate readings (probably due to low battery) and it worked quite well for a while. Unfortunately, it didn’t turn off automatically after 15 minutes as it’s supposed to and quickly drained the batteries. Maybe I just got a bad unit, but it’s going to cost me too much in batteries to keep using it.
